business_problem: Benete needed a way to turn large volumes of BeneCare assisted-daily-living sensor data into usable caregiver insights without forcing nurses and care teams to manually interpret dashboards and create summaries.
solution_summary: Benete worked with IBM Client Engineering to add an LLM-based summarization layer to its BeneCare elder-care platform. IoT sensors already captured activity, movement, sleep, hygiene, and food-preparation signals for elderly clients; IBM watsonx.ai was introduced to convert that raw operational data into concise care summaries and multilingual reports. Benete created prompt templates in watsonx.ai, used IBM Cloudant to store structured sensor findings and generated summaries, and tracked model development with Jupyter Notebook plus AI factsheets in IBM watsonx.governance. Llama and Mistral models were evaluated and then deployed on watsonx.ai as endpoints that transform the incoming care data into readable insights integrated back into BeneCare. This architecture preserves the continuous monitoring workflow while automating the most time-consuming interpretation step for caregivers.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Hosts the prompt-driven LLM endpoints that turn care data into readable summaries and translations.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloudant
solution_components.role: Stores structured IoT-derived findings and the generated summaries for efficient retrieval and querying.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.governance
solution_components.role: Tracks AI factsheets and evaluation artifacts so Benete can monitor prompt and model behavior.

solution_components.name: Llama
solution_components.role: Provides one of the large language models Benete evaluated and deployed for summary generation.

solution_components.name: Mistral
solution_components.role: Provides an alternative large language model Benete deployed to keep the summarization capability model-agnostic.

data_flow: IoT sensors feed BeneCare with assisted-daily-living data, Benete stores structured findings in IBM Cloudant, prompt templates in IBM watsonx.ai call Llama or Mistral endpoints to generate summaries and translations, and the resulting outputs are pushed back into BeneCare dashboards for caregivers and nurses.
business_outcome: Benete gave caregivers near-instant, multilingual summaries of client conditions, sharply reduced the time needed to interpret patient data, and improved the ability to deliver preventive care while serving more elderly clients efficiently.
